_note: Plain-English definitions used by every agent. Agents may define terms only from this file. Approved by Micah on 2026-11-22.

surplus.label: Surplus
surplus.plain: What the company owns minus what it owes policyholders and others. The cushion that protects policyholders when things go wrong.

asset_liability_management.label: Asset liability management (ALM)
asset_liability_management.plain: Choosing investments so they behave like the promises made to policyholders, so that market moves change both sides by similar amounts.

duration.label: Duration
duration.plain: How sensitive a value is to interest rates. A duration of 7 means the value falls about 7% if rates rise 1 percentage point, and rises about 7% if they fall 1 point.

duration_gap.label: Rate mismatch (duration gap)
duration_gap.plain: The difference between how rate-sensitive the assets are and how rate-sensitive the liabilities are, expressed in years. A gap means surplus moves when rates move.

dv01.label: DV01
dv01.plain: The dollar change in value for a 0.01 percentage point (one basis point) move in interest rates.

basis_point.label: Basis point (bp)
basis_point.plain: One hundredth of a percentage point. 100 basis points = 1%.

convexity.label: Convexity
convexity.plain: The bend in the price-to-rate relationship: for big rate moves, duration alone slightly misstates the change in value.

interest_rate_swap.label: Interest rate swap
interest_rate_swap.plain: A contract to exchange fixed interest payments for floating ones. Receiving fixed gains value when rates fall, so it can make assets behave more like long liabilities.

surrender.label: Surrender (lapse)
surrender.plain: A policyholder cashing out an annuity or policy early. Surrenders rise when competitors offer higher rates, and the insurer must pay out cash.

crediting_rate.label: Crediting rate
crediting_rate.plain: The interest rate the insurer pays on an annuity account. If market rates climb well above it, policyholders are tempted to surrender.

surrender_charge.label: Surrender charge / market value adjustment
surrender_charge.plain: A fee or adjustment when a policyholder leaves early. It protects the insurer from part of the loss of paying out when rates have risen.

margin_call.label: Margin call
margin_call.plain: A demand to post cash collateral because a derivative has lost value. It must be paid quickly, even if the loss is only on paper.

liquidity_ratio.label: Liquidity ratio
liquidity_ratio.plain: Cash and easily sold government bonds divided by the cash the company might need in a 90-day stress. Below 100% means it could be forced to sell other assets at a loss.

forced_selling.label: Forced selling
forced_selling.plain: Selling investments because cash is needed now, not because it is a good time. In a stressed market this means accepting a discount (a haircut).

liquidity_haircut.label: Haircut
liquidity_haircut.plain: The discount accepted when selling an investment quickly. Haircuts get much bigger when markets are stressed.

capital_ratio.label: Capital ratio (simplified)
capital_ratio.plain: Surplus divided by a simplified capital requirement that grows with riskier assets and liabilities. Below 100% is a breach. This game's version is a teaching simplification, not the regulatory RBC ratio.

credit_spread.label: Credit spread
credit_spread.plain: The extra yield a bond pays over a government bond for the risk that the borrower does not pay. When spreads widen, bond prices fall even if nobody defaults.

default.label: Default
default.plain: A borrower failing to pay. Unlike a spread move, a default is a permanent loss, softened only by what is recovered.

investment_grade.label: Investment grade (AAA, A, BBB)
investment_grade.plain: Bonds rated BBB or better. In this game AAA bonds never default, A bonds lose 15% as much as BBB bonds, and BBB bonds take the full credit loss on the card.

below_investment_grade.label: Below investment grade (junk bonds)
below_investment_grade.plain: Bonds rated below BBB. They pay more interest but default far more often, especially in a recession.

mortgage_loan.label: Commercial mortgage loans
mortgage_loan.plain: Loans the insurer makes against office buildings, warehouses, apartments and similar property. Hard to sell quickly.

alternatives.label: Alternatives (incl. stocks)
alternatives.plain: Private equity, real estate funds, hedge funds and stocks. They earn more over time and are deliberately left unhedged so the company keeps that extra return, but they fall when markets fall.

equity_risk_premium.label: Equity risk premium
equity_risk_premium.plain: The extra return investors expect for owning risky assets like stocks instead of safe bonds. Hedging it away would give up the return insurers rely on to fund future claims.

variable_annuity_guarantee.label: Stock-market guarantee (VA guarantee)
variable_annuity_guarantee.plain: A promise that a policyholder's account invested in the market will not fall below a set amount. When stocks or rates fall, the insurer owes more under the promise.

separate_account.label: Separate account
separate_account.plain: Money invested on behalf of policyholders, mostly at their own risk. Only the guarantees written on it are the insurer's risk.

put_option.label: Put option
put_option.plain: Insurance against a market fall: it pays out if stocks drop below a set level. It costs a premium every quarter whether or not it pays.

fx_hedge.label: Currency hedge
fx_hedge.plain: A trade that offsets losses on foreign assets when the dollar strengthens. It costs a little every quarter.

forward_contract.label: Forward contract
forward_contract.plain: An agreement to exchange currencies later at a rate fixed today. Used to lock in the dollar value of foreign assets.

counterparty_risk.label: Counterparty risk
counterparty_risk.plain: The risk that the bank on the other side of a hedge fails and does not pay what it owes.

collateral.label: Collateral
collateral.plain: Cash or bonds posted to cover what one side of a derivative owes the other. With daily collateral, a dealer's failure costs little.

isda_csa.label: ISDA / CSA
isda_csa.plain: The standard legal agreements for derivatives. The CSA (credit support annex) sets the collateral rules.

replacement_cost.label: Replacement cost
replacement_cost.plain: What it costs to set up the same hedge again with a new dealer after the old one fails, at today's market prices.

pension_risk_transfer.label: Pension risk transfer (PRT)
pension_risk_transfer.plain: An insurer taking over a company's pension promises in exchange for a premium. It brings long liabilities that must be matched with long assets.

carry.label: Carry
carry.plain: Investment income minus the interest credited to policyholders, expenses and hedge costs over a quarter. How the company earns money when markets are calm.

hedge_ratio.label: Hedge ratio
hedge_ratio.plain: The share of a risk that a hedge offsets. 100% removes the risk but costs the most; most companies hedge a large share, not all.

aoci.label: AOCI
aoci.plain: Accumulated other comprehensive income: unrealized gains and losses on bonds. This game measures surplus excluding AOCI, because insurers usually hold bonds to maturity.
